hook: Alone in a dinghy at night, drifting away from a sinking boat.
narration: She was alone in a dinghy at night, ten miles off Puerto Rico, and her boat was going down.
At seven twenty four p.m., the catamaran Blue Cocktail sent a mayday. It was taking on water and rapidly sinking.
She drifted off in the dinghy. He fought the flooding until he had to abandon ship.
A Coast Guard plane found the man in the water and the woman in the dinghy. A helicopter guided a response boat to them.
outcome: Both boaters, in life jackets, were rescued and taken to San Juan with no medical concerns.
title: Adrift in a dinghy as her boat sank
description:
A Coast Guard Station San Juan boat crew rescues two people after the catamaran Blue Cocktail took on water and sank about 10 miles north of Manati, Puerto Rico, on Dec. 6, 2019.

extra_sources.excerpt: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Coast Guard air and surface crews and the crew of the passenger ferry Kydon combined efforts to rescue two boaters from a sinking catamaran Friday night, approximately 10 nautical miles north of Manati, Puerto Rico.
Watchstanders at Sector San Juan received at 7:24 p.m. Friday a mayday radio call from the Blue Cocktail, on VHF Channel 16, reporting the vessel was taking on water and rapidly sinking.

Shortly after the initial distress call, the woman jumped on the dinghy which started drifting away from the catamaran, while the man stayed onboard attempting to control the flooding. The man was forced to abandon the vessel as it started to sink and became partially submerged.

Upon arriving on scene, the crew of the HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircraft located the man in the water and the woman safely aboard the dinghy.  The Coast Guard helicopter arrived on scene shortly thereafter and the aircrew vectored-in the Coast Guard response boat to the survivors' position.
The mariners in this case were doubly prepared with life jackets which they donned when directed by the Coast Guard.  Be prepared when recreating on the water, there is no room for errors at sea.
Following the rescue, the survivors were transported to San Juan and transferred to Customs and Border Protection personnel with no medical concerns
